title: Planetary transits (gochar) explained, and read from the Moon | Ask Tota
description: Classical gochar is counted from your Moon sign, not your ascendant. Here are the favourable houses for every graha, the vedha rule nobody mentions, and the base rate.
og_title: Transits are read from ur moon, not ur lagna

llms_desc: why classical gochar counts from the Moon sign rather than the lagna, the favourable houses for each graha, the vedha cancellation, ashtakavarga bindus, and the double transit rule.

faq.a: the sanskrit term for transit: where the grahas are in the sky right now, read against ur birth chart. it is the background weather of a chart, as opposed to the dasha, which is the schedule.

faq.q: are transits read from the lagna or the moon?
faq.a: classical gochar is counted from the moon sign. that is the tradition's own convention and it is the single most common thing modern transit content gets wrong.

faq.q: why the moon and not the ascendant?
faq.a: gochar is a system about the mind's response to conditions, and the moon carries the mind. it also means the reading works without a birth time, which matters in a tradition where exact times were often unavailable.

faq.q: which houses are favourable for each graha?
faq.a: counted from the moon: the sun is favourable in 3, 6, 10 and 11. the moon in 1, 3, 6, 7, 10 and 11. mars in 3, 6 and 11. mercury in 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 and 11. jupiter in 2, 5, 7, 9 and 11. venus in 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 8, 9, 11 and 12. saturn in 3, 6 and 11.

an obstruction. if another graha occupies a specific counterpart house at the same time, the transit result is cancelled. it is a core part of the classical system and it is left out of nearly every popular transit reading.

faq.q: what is the double transit rule?
faq.a: a house is treated as genuinely activated when jupiter and saturn both influence it at the same time, by sitting in it or aspecting it. because their speeds differ so much, that is uncommon and short, which is why it carries weight.

faq.q: what is ashtakavarga and how does it refine transits?
faq.a: a points system giving each sign a score from each graha's perspective, out of eight. a transit through a sign with a high bindu count is read as easier than the same transit through a low-scoring sign, which personalises a result that would otherwise apply to everybody.

faq.q: how many people share a transit result with me?
faq.a: roughly a twelfth of everyone alive, because gochar is counted from the moon sign and there are twelve of those. that is the number that keeps any transit claim in proportion.

the slow ones. saturn at about 2.5 years per sign, jupiter at about a year, and the rahu ketu axis at about 18 months. the moon changes sign every 2.25 days and mercury moves constantly, so those are day-to-day weather rather than chapters.

faq.q: is a transit more important than a dasha?
faq.a: no, and the tradition is clear about this. dashas are the timing engine and run in chunks of years. transits describe conditions. a transit is generally read as triggering something the dasha has already made available.

faq.q: does a bad transit mean something bad will happen?
faq.a: it describes a condition that applies to a twelfth of the population simultaneously. what it produces in one life depends on the chart underneath it, the dasha running, and a great many things astrology never claimed to see.

faq.q: what is the difference between gochar and the natal chart?
faq.a: the natal chart is fixed at birth and never changes. gochar is where the grahas are today. one is who u are, the other is what the weather is doing, and confusing them is the commonest error in transit content.
